bullets: Mispronunciation is a high-signal mistake — it tells listeners 'this person isn't paying attention', making it more damaging than its apparent size suggests.
Reliability of voice is partly preparation, partly humility; neither alone is sufficient to earn listener trust.
The mispronunciation pattern has played out at teams using NPR and held consistently across three different teams rather than being a one-off observation.
The second-order effect of these credibility signals is the part most people miss — small lapses compound into broader doubts about attention and care.
Ignoring the preparation-and-humility foundation of reliability means rebuilding it from scratch a year later rather than maintaining it incrementally.
Trade-offs around reliability cross-cut every other aspect of public radio, including where journalism and public radio intersect and how outlets like BBC fit the picture.
Practical adoption starts small — pick one idea and run it for two weeks, treating everything after that as iteration rather than a fixed plan.
